newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open higher Thursday after five days of gains took prices back up toward the eigh- month high set in early March.

Renewed tightness in the prompt market, shortcovering by funds after prices became oversold again, news some workers at Chile's Escondida mine had voted to continue their strike, and news the Kennecott smelter in Utah will stop producing blister for another five weeks, were all behind the firm tone, traders said.
COMEX May copper was called unchanged to up 0.5 cent from Wednesday's close of 112.80 cents a lb after trading from 112.80 to 113.80 cents on ACCESS.
Resistance in the May contract is pagged around 114.00 cents, a level seen briefly in early March.

The May/July spread has widened sharply again this week to around 2.70 cents, from 1.00 cent in mid-April, while on the LME the cash-to-three months spread was back out around $200 a tonne from below $50 a tonne in mid-April.
LME warehouse copper stocks fell 2,350 tonnes Thursday to 146,750 tonnes, while COMEX stocks rose 1,448 short tons Wednesday to 50,181 short tons.
